From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Fossò

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From fossa. Compare with Neapolitan fuosso.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈfɔs.so/
  • Rhymes: -ɔsso
  • Hyphenation: fòs‧so

Noun

[edit]

fosso m (plural fossi)

  1. ditch
  2. moat

Derived terms

[edit]
  • refosso / rifosso

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Spanish: foso

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *bʰedʰh₂-der.
Proto-Indo-European *bʰódʰh₂ey
Proto-Italic *foðjō
Latin fodiō
Latin fossō

    Frequentative of fodiō (“to dig, to excavate; to mine”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈfɔs.soː]
    • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈfɔs.so]

    Verb

    [edit]

    fossō (present infinitive fossāre, perfect active fossāvī, supine fossātum); first conjugation

    1. (with the sense of being done often) to dig, pierce

    Portuguese

    [edit]

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    Possibly an alteration of fossa (“hole, cavity”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
     
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfo.su/
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfo.su/
      • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfo.so/
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈfo.su/

    Noun

    [edit]

    fosso m (plural fossos, metaphonic)

    1. ditch, trench

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfɔ.su/
      • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfɔ.so/
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈfɔ.su/
